subject: Geography
description: Himalayas, Aravallis, Vindhyas, Western/Eastern Ghats, Satpura

questions.stem: The highest peak lying entirely within India is:

options.option_text: Mount Everest
Kanchenjunga
Nanda Devi
K2

questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) — third-highest in the world — lies on the India-Nepal border with its main peak in Sikkim. Everest (8,849 m) straddles Nepal-China, not Indian territory. K2 (8,611 m) lies in the Pakistan-administered part of Kashmir. Nanda Devi (7,816 m in Uttarakhand) is the highest peak entirely within undisputed Indian territory.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Aravalli range, one of the oldest fold mountains in the world, runs through which state?

options.option_text: Uttar Pradesh
Rajasthan
Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra

questions.explanation: The Aravallis run ~670 km mainly through Rajasthan (from Palanpur in Gujarat to Delhi, via Udaipur, Ajmer, Alwar). Highest peak: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu. These are among the world's oldest mountains (Proterozoic age, ~350 million years older than the Himalayas), heavily eroded today. They separate the Thar desert from the Ganga plain.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The highest peak in the Western Ghats (and of peninsular India) is:

options.option_text: Doddabetta
Anamudi
Mahendragiri
Vindhyachal

questions.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala's Eravikulam National Park is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India. Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest in the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu). Mahendragiri (1,501 m) lies in the Eastern Ghats of Odisha. 'Vindhyachal' is another name for the Vindhya range, not a single peak.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the mountain range with the state it chiefly runs through. A. Satpura. B. Vindhya. C. Zaskar. D. Karakoram. List-II: 1. Madhya Pradesh, 2. MP/Uttar Pradesh border, 3. Ladakh (J&K), 4. Ladakh (disputed PoK).
questions.explanation: Satpura — Madhya Pradesh; separates the Narmada and Tapi rivers. Vindhya — Madhya Pradesh/UP border; separates northern and peninsular India. Zaskar — an eastern Himalayan range largely within Ladakh. Karakoram — contains K2 and several 8,000-m peaks; parts pass through Gilgit-Baltistan (PoK) and Aksai Chin (disputed with China).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Himalayan range divides into three parallel mountain belts. The northernmost and highest belt is called the:

options.option_text: Shiwaliks
Great Himalayas (Himadri)
Lesser Himalayas (Himachal)
Purvanchal

questions.explanation: The Himalayas have three longitudinal belts — from north to south: Himadri (Great Himalayas) with the highest peaks (Everest, Kanchenjunga), Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) in the middle with hill stations like Shimla and Darjeeling, and Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas) — youngest, lowest. Purvanchal is the eastern offshoot running into NE India (Patkai, Naga, Mizo and Manipur hills).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats meet at the:

options.option_text: Palghat Gap
Nilgiri Hills
Satpura range
Cardamom Hills

questions.explanation: The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats converge in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu. The Palghat Gap (Palakkad) is a pass through the Western Ghats that connects Kerala and Tamil Nadu, not a meeting point of the two Ghats. Cardamom Hills lie further south in the Western Ghats. Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is the famous hill station in the Nilgiris.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Mount K2, the second-highest peak in the world, lies in which mountain range?

options.option_text: Great Himalayas
Karakoram
Hindu Kush
Pamirs

questions.explanation: K2 (8,611 m) — after Everest (8,849 m) the second-highest peak — lies in the Karakoram range, on the China-Pakistan border within the disputed region of Gilgit-Baltistan (which India claims as part of J&K). Four of the world's 14 'eight-thousanders' are in the Karakoram. Hindu Kush lies chiefly in Afghanistan; Pamirs straddle Tajikistan, Afghanistan and China.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The longitudinal flat-floored valleys lying between the Shivalik hills and the Lesser Himalayas are locally referred to as?

options.option_text: Duars — lowland corridors along Assam and West Bengal foothills
Duns — elongated flat valleys such as Dehradun and Patlidun
Bhurs — sandy wind-blown hillocks found in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab
Karewas — ancient lake-bed terraces found in the Kashmir Valley

questions.explanation: Duns (or Doons) are elongated valleys formed between the Shivaliks and the Lesser Himalayas — Dehradun, Patlidun, and Kotlidun are classic examples. Duars are the alluvial lowland corridors at the base of the Eastern Himalayas in West Bengal and Assam, not between two Himalayan ranges. Karewas are lacustrine terraces unique to the Kashmir Valley, while Bhurs are Ganga plain features, making both irrelevant here.

questions.stem: Patkai, Naga, Mizo (Lushai), and Manipur hills together constitute which hill system running along India's northeastern frontier?

options.option_text: Purvanchal Hills — the north-south curving ranges of Northeast India
Meghalaya Plateau — the detached Precambrian block between Assam and Bengal
Arakan Yoma — the main north-south mountain chain running through Myanmar
Eastern Ghats — the discontinuous range along India's southeastern coast

questions.explanation: The Patkai, Naga, Mizo (Lushai), and Manipur hills collectively form the Purvanchal range, India's northeastern border ranges with Myanmar. A common confusion is with the Arakan Yoma: while Purvanchal hills are structural extensions of the Arakan Yoma into India, the Arakan Yoma itself lies within Myanmar. The Meghalaya Plateau (Shillong Plateau) is a separate detached Peninsular block, not part of this northeastern hill arc.

questions.stem: The Pir Panjal range, which lies south of the Kashmir Valley and intercepts the southwest monsoon creating a rain shadow over the valley, belongs to which Himalayan zone?

options.option_text: Himadri (Greater Himalayas) — the northernmost, highest crystalline belt
Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) — the middle zone with elevations 3,700–4,500 m
Shivalik (Outer Himalayas) — the youngest and southernmost foothill belt
Trans-Himalayas (Tethys zone) — the dry plateau belt north of the main range

questions.explanation: The Pir Panjal is the most prominent sub-range of the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal zone), running through Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh. It is the largest range within this middle belt. A common error is placing it in the Himadri (Greater Himalayas) because it is topographically prominent, but Himadri contains the main crystalline peaks above 6,000 m; Pir Panjal peaks average around 4,000–5,000 m, squarely in the Himachal zone.

questions.stem: The Cardamom Hills, a major spice-growing belt straddling Kerala and Tamil Nadu, form part of the southern section of which mountain range?

options.option_text: Eastern Ghats — the discontinuous hill range along India's eastern coast
Nilgiri Hills — the junction block where Eastern and Western Ghats converge
Western Ghats (Sahyadri) — the continuous escarpment along India's west coast
Satpura Range — the east-west trending horst range of central India

questions.explanation: The Cardamom Hills (also called Kannan Devan Hills) in Idukki district of Kerala are part of the Western Ghats' southern section, lying south of the Anaimalai Hills. The tempting distractor is the Nilgiri Hills, since the Nilgiris are geographically nearby and are where Eastern and Western Ghats meet — but the Cardamom Hills are distinctly south of the Nilgiris and belong to the Western Ghats continuity, not the Nilgiri block itself.

questions.stem: Khardung La, a high-altitude pass in Ladakh, connects Leh to which valley and is strategically vital for supplying which military zone?

options.option_text: Spiti Valley in Himachal Pradesh — for supplying the Rohtang sector posts
Nubra Valley in Ladakh — for supplying the Siachen Glacier base camps
Zanskar Valley in Ladakh — for supplying the Kargil sector outposts
Shyok Valley in Ladakh — for accessing the Daulat Beg Oldie airstrip

questions.explanation: Khardung La (5,359 m) connects Leh to the Nubra Valley, serving as the primary supply route for the Indian Army's Siachen Glacier operations. Zanskar and Spiti are connected via different passes (Pensi La and Rohtang/Kunzum respectively). Shyok Valley is a common confusion because the Siachen area is drained by the Shyok river system, but the actual pass used for Siachen logistics is Khardung La leading first to Nubra, then onward.

questions.stem: The 'Dihang Gorge,' one of the world's deepest gorges marking the eastern syntaxis of the Himalayas, is carved by which river as it turns sharply southward around the peak of Namcha Barwa?

options.option_text: Teesta River — draining the Sikkim and Darjeeling Himalayan section southward
Brahmaputra (Tsangpo-Siang) — looping around Namcha Barwa before entering Arunachal Pradesh
Lohit River — an eastern tributary joining Brahmaputra near the Assam plains
Subansiri River — draining the central Arunachal-Tibet watershed into Assam

questions.explanation: The Tsangpo river of Tibet makes a dramatic hairpin turn around Namcha Barwa (7,782 m) — the eastern anchor (syntaxis) of the Himalayan arc — carving the Yarlung Tsangpo / Dihang Gorge, deeper than the Grand Canyon. It then enters Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang/Dihang before becoming the Brahmaputra. The Lohit is a frequent distractor because it also originates in Tibet and joins the Brahmaputra, but it does not loop around Namcha Barwa and forms no famous gorge.

questions.stem: The 'Karewas' of the Kashmir Valley are geologically ancient lake-bed (lacustrine) deposits. These terraces are agriculturally prized for cultivation of which GI-tagged crop that cannot be grown on ordinary paddy-field soil?

options.option_text: Apple orchards — grown on well-drained loamy Karewa soils above the valley floor
Saffron (Kesar) — uniquely cultivated on Karewa terraces in Pampore, Pulwama
Walnut plantations — grown on the clay-rich terraces near Sopore and Baramulla
Paddy (rice) — grown in the waterlogged low-lying Karewa depressions near Dal Lake

questions.explanation: Kashmir saffron (GI tag awarded in 2020) is exclusively grown on Karewa terraces — particularly in Pampore tehsil, Pulwama — because saffron crocus requires well-drained, slightly calcareous, flat plateau soil, conditions uniquely provided by the ancient lake-bed Karewa deposits. Waterlogged paddy soil is actually unsuitable for saffron. Apples and walnuts are also important Kashmiri crops but are grown on hill slopes and alluvial soils, not specifically on Karewas — making them plausible but wrong distractors.
